_comment: ABI of BLSAggregator-4.11.0 AS DEPLOYED on Sepolia at 0xEaeC2F512eA50708211fa95533e4dBb60e3d2E5D. abis/BLSAggregator.json tracks contracts/src, which is 4.12.0 (#400) and NOT on any chain: BLSAggregator is not upgradeable, so 4.12.0 would need a fresh deploy plus another three-leg rotation. Pin THIS file for anything that talks to the deployed contract. Measured 2026-09-04: guardianSlashBps() reverts on chain while GUARDIAN_SLASH_CASE_WINDOW() and version() answer, so the difference is real and not an RPC artifact. Two kinds of drift are recorded below: notInDeployed_presentIn_4_12_0 (calls that revert) and changedShape_sameSelector (calls that decode wrongly).

guardianSlashCases(uint256).note: #400 inserted uint16 slashBps into GuardianSlashCase, so the public getter gained a return value. The SELECTOR IS UNCHANGED. Measured on chain 2026-09-04: the call returns 224 bytes = 7 words; decoding it with the 4.11.0 shape succeeds, decoding the SAME bytes with the 4.12.0 shape fails with 'buffer overrun while deserializing'. This is the more dangerous half of the drift -- an absent function reverts loudly, a changed return shape misdecodes. The first version of this file listed only the four added functions and would have let a consumer believe the rest was compatible. Found by Codex.
